chapter: Touring shows and the bands he heard
title: Hearing the bands on nationwide radio and at dances
summary: Benny Goodman's Camel Caravan, Henderson and Hines from the Grand Terrace, territorial bands, and free admission to dances as a local musician.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Then I had the opportunity to play the World's Fair in 1964, and I told Benny how I used to go to the ice cream parlor and listen to him every Wednesday night at 7:30 on the Camel Caravan -- a show that he broadcast from New York called the Camel Caravan. I'd go over there to the ice cream parlor, and they had a little radio sitting in the window; I'd go over there and listen to him play on the Camel Caravan at ...(?)..

And then, late at night, we'd get Fletcher Henderson and Earl Fatha Hines; we'd get them from the Grand Terrace in Chicago. And we could also get Cab Calloway and Duke Ellington from the Cotton Club, you see... All of this was nationwide radio during those days, you know...

I got to hear a lot of music! A lot of different bands, like Jeter-Philips out of St. Louis, and Don Albert out of San Antonio, Texas... Oh, all kind of bands, territorial bands that I had the opportunity to hear. The Carolina Cotton Pickers; Cat Anderson was with that band, out of Jenkins Orphanage in South Carolina. And all kind of bands. Joe Robicheaux out of New Orleans. Henry

Desvignes. All kind of bands came through.
And by me being a musician, ha-ha!, they would let me come to the dances. I could go in free and listen to the bands. So I could get a chance to hear everybody. I was the only kid in the place, but I could hear everybody -- they'd let me in. Because they all knew me around home, you know. Everybody knew me. And it really enhanced me. It enhanced me...

Oh, yeah. Well, I would be there for business, you know. I was there to listen, you know. Because I wasn't a dancer by any stretch of the imagination! I had trouble tapping my foot in time! But it was really nice.
